title: Security and Safety —

header.html: Keep secrets out of a repository with .gitignore and environment variables; respond to a committed secret by rotating, amending, rewriting history and force pushing; find a secret with git log -S; explain secret scanning, push protection and Dependabot; sign commits with an SSH key and verify them; harden a workflow by pinning actions, limiting permissions and avoiding script injection

toc.title: Keep secrets out of the repository
A secret was committed: rotate first
What GitHub adds: scanning, protection, Dependabot, signing

html:
1Keep secrets out of the repository

A secret is anything that grants access: a token, an API key, a private key, a login. Git remembers everything, so a secret committed once lives in the history of every clone. The figure shows the layers of defense.

Do Do not
Read secrets from environment variables Write secrets in code, config files, commit messages or issues
Keep local values in a .env file that .gitignore lists Commit .env; commit a .env.example with fake placeholders instead
Keep shared values in a secret store, such as Actions secrets Put a token in a remote URL: it is saved as plain text in .git/config

.gitignore only affects files that Git does not track yet. A file that is already tracked stays tracked until you run git rm --cached on it.

Tip

. Add .env to .gitignore before the first commit, and commit a .env.example with fake values. New teammates learn the variable names and never see a real secret.

2A secret was committed: rotate first

The order matters. Rotate the credential first: create a new one and revoke the old one at the service that issued it. Only then clean the history. A secret that reached a shared repository must be treated as leaked, because clones, forks and caches keep copies even after you delete it.

Situation What to do
Last commit, not pushed git rm --cached the file, then git commit --amend
Older commit, or already pushed Rewrite every commit with git filter-repo or the BFG Repo-Cleaner, then force push with --force-with-lease; teammates must re-clone or reset
Pushed to a shared repository Rotate anyway: rewriting history is cleanup, not a cure

To find a secret, git log -S"text" lists the commits that add or remove that exact text. Try it: the last commit added .env with a fake key. Your hashes will differ.

git log -S"demo-9f8e7d6c" --oneline
echo ".env" >> .gitignore
git rm --cached .env
git add .gitignore
git commit --amend -m "Add shop config"
git log -S"demo-9f8e7d6c" --oneline
git show HEAD@{1}:.env

043059b Add shop config
rm '.env'
[main 3527f3d] Add shop config
API_KEY=demo-9f8e7d6c5b4a

The output is trimmed: the amend prints more lines, and the second search prints nothing because the branch no longer holds the key. The old commit still sits in the reflog (module 6), which the last command reads, and on any clone that already fetched it. That is why the rotation comes first.

Tip

. Rotate the credential before you touch the history. Cleaning takes time, and a leaked key can be used the whole time.

3What GitHub adds: scanning, protection, Dependabot, signing

Feature What it does Good to know
Secret scanning Scans the full history of every branch, and also issues, pull requests, discussions and wikis Free for public repositories; private and internal organization repositories need GitHub Secret Protection
Push protection Blocks a push that contains a detected secret For users, on by default in public repositories; for repositories it needs GitHub Secret Protection and is off by default
Dependabot alerts Warn about vulnerable dependencies when a new advisory is added or the dependency graph changes Scan the default branch; admins and organization owners enable them
Dependabot version updates Open pull requests that keep dependencies and actions current You choose what to watch

Anyone with write access can override a push protection block by default, and must give a reason. "It's used in tests" and "It's a false positive" create closed alerts; "I'll fix it later" creates an open alert. When an alert names a real credential, rotate it. Dependabot alerts for Actions cover only semantic versions, not SHA pins.

Signed commits prove who made a commit. Git can sign with GPG, S/MIME or, since Git 2.34, an SSH key. GitHub shows a Verified badge when it can check the signature, and Unverified when it cannot; an unsigned commit shows no status. A branch protection rule can require signed commits. Commits made in the web interface are signed by GitHub itself, but rebase and merge commits are not.

ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N "" -C ada@example.com -f ada_key
echo "ada@example.com $(cat ada_key.pub)" > allowed_signers
git config gpg.format ssh
git config user.signingkey "$PWD/ada_key.pub"
git config gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile "$PWD/allowed_signers"
git config commit.gpgsign true
git commit --allow-empty -m "Signed commit"
git verify-commit HEAD
git log --show-signature -1

Good "git" signature for ada@example.com with ED25519 key SHA256:LT5GpHLNDXRLSKph3ey8eVNlIM8pbqKTshJUbduFmZ8
commit d5a942a9b18b21a1b337c3306b930d44111a4cf1
Good "git" signature for ada@example.com with ED25519 key SHA256:LT5GpHLNDXRLSKph3ey8eVNlIM8pbqKTshJUbduFmZ8
Author: Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>

    Signed commit

The empty -N means no protection for the private key, and the key sits next to the code: both are only for this lab. In real life keep the key in your .ssh folder, protect it with a phrase and add its public half to your GitHub account.

The allowed signers file lists whom your local Git trusts, and verify-commit fails without it.

Tip

. Turn on push protection. Blocking a secret before the push is far cheaper than rotating it and cleaning the history afterwards.

4Safer Actions and token hygiene

A workflow runs code with access to your repository, so a careless line can leak a secret or run an attacker's code.

Risk Rule
Third-party actions Pin to a full commit SHA, because a tag can be moved; a tag is fine only for creators you trust
Token rights Least privilege: read contents by default and raise it per job
Untrusted text Never write ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} inside run:; GitHub pastes it into the script text, so a title can add commands. Hand it over through env:
pull_request_target Runs in the context of the base repository, so avoid it unless needed and never check out the pull request code under it
Self-hosted runners Almost never on public repositories
Cloud credentials Prefer OIDC to long-lived keys
Changes to workflows CODEOWNERS can require review for .github/workflows; Dependabot version updates keep pinned actions current 
# .github/workflows/safe.yml
on: pull_request
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      # example only: use the full commit SHA of a release you reviewed
      - uses: octo-org/lint-action@3d1f5a8c9e2b4a7d6c0f1e8b9a2d3c4e5f6a7b8c
      - run: echo "Title is $TITLE"
        env: {TITLE: "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"}

Token hygiene. Prefer a fine-grained personal access token: one owner, only the repositories it needs and granular permissions. A classic token with the repo scope reaches every repository you can reach.

Keep tokens out of remote URLs, scripts and chats. Let SSH or a credential helper such as Git Credential Manager hold them, and use the short-lived GITHUB_TOKEN inside workflows. Revoke tokens you no longer use.

5Practice Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1You committed .env with a live API key as your last commit and have not pushed. What is the best first step?

  • ARun git commit --amend before anyone sees the commit
  • BDelete the file in a new commit and push it quickly
  • CRotate the key at the service, then fix the commit
  • DAdd .env to .gitignore and carry on working
Show the answer

Answer: C. A secret that was committed must be rotated first, because the old commit may still be copied or read.

S2A key was pushed to main yesterday and teammates pulled it. You amend, force push and delete the file. Is the key safe now?

  • AYes, a force push erases every copy of the old commit
  • BYes, GitHub removes old commits right after a force push
  • CNo, the key is only unsafe until the next merge
  • DNo, clones and forks may still hold the old commit
Show the answer

Answer: D. Copies of a pushed commit can live in clones, forks and caches, so the key must be treated as leaked and rotated.

S3git log -S"demo-9f8e7d6c" --oneline prints two commits: 9c2e41a Remove key and 4b7d0f3 Add config. What does this show?

  • AThe text appears in both commits but it never changes between them
  • BThe text was added in one commit and removed in the other
  • CThe text is still in the working tree of both commits
  • DThe text was moved to another file in the later commit
Show the answer

Answer: B. -S lists commits that add or remove the text, so the key is still in the history.

S4With gpg.format ssh and a signing key set, git verify-commit HEAD fails with an error about a missing file. What is missing?

  • AA gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile that lists the trusted keys
  • BA GPG key ring that holds the public key of the author
  • CA push to GitHub so that the signature is checked online
  • DA commit.gpgsign setting that is switched off again
Show the answer

Answer: A. Local verification of SSH signatures needs an allowed signers file with the trusted public keys.

S5A workflow has run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}". A contributor names a pull request with shell commands in it. What is the risk and the fix?

  • AThe title is cut at fifty characters, so use a longer shell
  • BThe title's commands run, so hand it over through env:
  • CThe step fails on quotes, so use single quotes in the script
  • DOnly the title is printed, so the step is already safe to use
Show the answer

Answer: B. GitHub pastes the title into the script text before the shell runs, so values should arrive through an environment variable.

S6A workflow uses octo-org/lint-action@v2, and the team fears the tag could be moved to bad code. What is the safest change?

  • APin the action to a full commit SHA of a reviewed version
  • BPin the action to the main branch of the same repository
  • CCopy the action name into a comment above the step
  • DSet permissions: read-all and keep the same tag
Show the answer

Answer: A. A full commit SHA cannot be moved, while tags and branches can.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What do you do first when a secret was pushed?

Show the answer

Rotate the credential at the service that issued it.

R2Which command lists the commits that add or remove a piece of text?

Show the answer

git log -S.

R3Which tools rewrite the history of every commit to remove a file?

Show the answer

git filter-repo or the BFG Repo-Cleaner.

R4Which setting makes Git sign commits with an SSH key?

Show the answer

gpg.format ssh, together with user.signingkey.

R5What does push protection do?

Show the answer

It blocks a push that contains a detected secret.

R6Which event needs care because it runs in the base repository context?

Show the answer

pull_request_target.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Keep out environment variables; .env in .gitignore; .env.example; secret stores; no tokens in URLs
